First tagged release. Inventario is a self-hosted personal inventory: what you own, where it is, what it cost, and the paperwork that came with it.

This is an **alpha for a small private cohort**, not a public launch. It is stable enough for daily use and does not lose data, but it has rough edges and gaps that are listed below rather than hidden.

## What it does

- **Structure.** Locations hold areas, areas hold commodities. Location groups scope everything, so several households or organizations can share one deployment without seeing each other's data.
- **Commodities.** Status tracking (in use, sold, lost, disposed, written off), purchase and registration dates, counts, serial numbers, free-form comments, and tags for filtering.
- **Money.** Original and current price per item, multiple currencies, and a per-group main currency with a migration path when you change it.
- **Files.** Images, manuals and invoices attach to items, locations and areas. Downloads go through time-limited signed URLs, so no authentication token is ever exposed in a link.
- **Search and reporting.** Full-text search across items, plus value and warranty views.
- **Import and export.** Whole-database backup and restore in a single `.inb` archive, and exports you can take elsewhere.
- **Accounts.** Password sign-in, passwordless magic links, TOTP two-factor, and OAuth identities. Invite-based membership with roles.
- **Administration.** A separate back-office for cross-tenant operations, with impersonation for support.
- **AI assist.** Optional scanning of an item photo to prefill the add-item form (Anthropic; off unless you configure it).

## Requirements

- PostgreSQL 13 or newer for any real deployment. The in-memory backend exists for trying things out and loses everything on restart.
- SMTP, if you want verification mail, password resets or invites to arrive. **The default email provider is a stub that silently drops mail** — configure a real one before inviting anyone.
- Kubernetes or Docker Compose. Both are supported and documented.

## First run

Set `JWT_SECRET` and `FILE_SIGNING_KEY` to your own values (`openssl rand -hex 32`) for anything reachable over a network. Left unset, the backend generates an ephemeral key on each start and every session dies with the process.

On Kubernetes the chart is not published to a chart repository — take it from this tag's checkout — and the image tag must be passed explicitly:

```bash
helm upgrade --install inventario ./helm/inventario \
  -n inventario -f values-prod.yaml --set image.tag=v0.1.0
```

## Known gaps

Honest list, each with its issue:

- The chart's `appVersion` is `latest`, which is not a published tag, so `--set image.tag=v0.1.0` is mandatory rather than optional ([#2035](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/2035)).
- No monitoring or alerting ships with the deployment ([#2034](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/2034)).
- Refresh tokens are not rotated and reuse is not detected ([#967](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/967)).
- The in-app support link returns 503 until `SUPPORT_EMAIL` is set ([#2103](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/2103)).
- The email-verification page can show "link expired" for a fresh token ([#2096](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/2096)).
- Several list pages render an empty state instead of an error when a request fails ([#2098](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/2098)).
- The admin and impersonation end-to-end suite is skipped, so that surface is covered by review rather than tests ([#2100](https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues/2100)).

There is no upgrade path to worry about yet — this is the first release, so there is nothing to upgrade from.

## Reporting

Issues are welcome at <https://github.com/denisvmedia/inventario/issues>. Say which of the two install paths you used and attach the server log; most first-run failures are configuration and the log usually names the setting.
